accuracy.evidence: Matches Development Matters (2021) Communication and Language: birth to 3 'sing songs and say rhymes' and 3 to 4 'anticipate key events and phrases in rhymes and stories'; refrain is defined as a repeated line with the same words. The four lines are checked against the traditional tales: Gingerbread Man 'Run, run, as fast as you can!', Three Little Pigs 'I'll huff and I'll puff', Billy Goats Gruff 'Who's that trip-trapping over my bridge?', Little Red Hen 'Not I'. Story pages 3 and 5 are the pauses (after the cow and horse say Stop); Teddy's pauses are pages 2, 4 and 6 of 7.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real early-joining-in slips named in the adult text: saying the line at every page instead of at the pause (Join in on a non-pause page is refused, m3, challenge 'when'), staying silent at the pause (Listen at a pause is refused, p3, challenge 'quiet'), changing the words (same-words scene, predict, p5, m8, challenge 'swap'), saying part of the line (dropped-word options, m4, challenge 'drop') and mixing up stories' lines (tale matching, p4, m2, challenge 'tale').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrefrain is a read-along book: pages turn one at a time and the child decides Join in or Listen on each, with the reader's pause shown; a meet-Stop-refrain order puzzle; four refrain bubbles dragged to traditional tales in shuffled order; a same-words picker against swapped and shortened versions; and a make-your-own refrain that the child then joins in with. It is not the rhymes-by-heart or predicting lessons; the lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child learns when to join in by doing it: a Join in on an ordinary page gets 'Not yet. Nobody stopped to wait for you', a Listen at a pause gets 'That is your turn'. The order puzzle makes the cue (Stop!) explicit, the same-words scene rejects changed words with the reason, and Teddy's story transfers the skill to a new line. The step summaries only confirm what the child just did.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'The end' after the pig says Stop (the order puzzle puts the refrain next) and 'Yes, new words each time' (the same-words scene shows only the identical line is accepted).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; wrong options carry five tagged messages: quiet (the pause is your turn), swap (same words every time), drop (say the whole line), tale (each story has its own line), when (the line comes at the pause, after Stop, not every page). Answer order rotates each question.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and the refrains themselves; on-canvas text is one story sentence per page and two big buttons (Join in, Listen) with pictures, suitable for a 2 to 3 year old with an adult reading. Curriculum terms (anticipate, phonological awareness) appear only in the adult text, within the validator limits.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: the Gingerbread Man's line and its cue; what a refrain is; your turn at the pause; each story has its own line. Adult paragraphs: curriculum placement, how to pause when reading, common mistakes, what the lab does. No stock phrases; the content gate's filler and duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the page card fills most of the width with a 16 px sentence, the Join in and Listen buttons are about half the width and over 100 px tall, tales and lines switch to a 2 x 2 grid on narrow screens, and the same-words options are full-width rows. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin (Join in, Listen, each order card, each line to each story, each same-words option, Teddy's three lines). The canvas aria-label reads each page sentence and every verdict; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes.

sources: DfE (2021) Development Matters: Communication and Language, birth to 3 and 3 and 4-year-olds (sing songs, say rhymes, anticipate key phrases)
DfE (2024) Statutory framework for the EYFS, ELG Comprehension and Speaking
BookTrust / Book Start guidance on reading aloud with toddlers: pause and let the child fill in the repeated line
Traditional tales: The Gingerbread Man, The Three Little Pigs, The Three Billy Goats Gruff, The Little Red Hen
